Listen to this article Share ​ Key players in Nigeria’s dairy sector are pushing regulators for clearer, unified product standards to eliminate consumer confusion and curb unfair competition in Africa’s largest consumer market. ​At a national roundtable in Lagos convened by the Danish Dairy Board, the Royal Danish consulate general, and dairy business partners, government officials and industry leaders called for precise definitions and classifications for dairy products, creamers, and fat-filled milk. ​The push comes as Nigeria seeks to modernize its food safety rules, boost domestic livestock investment, and crack down on mislabeled or substandard goods entering supply chains. ​”Realising this potential requires more than increasing local milk production; it also depends on a transparent regulatory framework that promotes product safety, protects consumers, encourages investment and supports fair competition,” said Idi Mukhtar Maiha, Nigeria’s minister of Livestock Development. ​Maiha noted that regulatory ambiguity makes market entry unpredictable for compliant operators while exacerbating broader challenges around counterfeit products across the agricultural and veterinary sectors. ​Regulators target labelling ​Discussions centered on harmonizing definitions across key oversight bodies—including the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC). ​NAFDAC reiterated its commitment to enforcing strict pre-packaged food labelling laws to prevent market misrepresentation. ​”The fundamental principle of food labelling… is to ensure that consumers are not misled,” said Chinyere Ikejiofor, head of nutrition and food safety at NAFDAC. “Product information must be clear and accurate, and products must not be described or presented in a manner that creates confusion about their nature, composition or characteristics.” ​EU-backed consumer push ​The dialogue forms part of the “Choose Milk” campaign, an initiative funded by the European Union and managed by the Danish Dairy Board aimed at improving consumer education and nutrition transparency in Nigeria. ​Lars Jensen, senior project manager at the Danish Dairy Board, emphasized that standardized labelling is vital for market confidence. Clear distinctions between pure dairy and alternative milk-based products enable consumers to make informed choices based on purchasing power while creating a level playing field for importers and local processors alike. ​Stakeholders concluded by advocating for sustained inter-agency coordination to reduce regulatory hurdles, protect public health, and accelerate investment across Nigeria’s dairy value chain.
